items.title: Australian EV owners deal with 'range anxiety'. China has almost eliminated it
items.description: In China you can swap an empty electric vehicle battery in about four minutes. It is part of how China has come to dominate the EV industry.

items.title: Prepare for stock market pain as China throws a spanner into AI boom
items.description: Elon Musk's latest venture sent global stock markets to dizzying heights, but its performance since does not augur well for the company or the future of the AI boom.

items.title: The four sets of data that show how the property market is transforming
items.description: Global instability, shifting tax policies and interest rate pressures force buyers and sellers to adjust to the changing property landscape.

items.title: 'Sit down!': Joyce's dog interrupts 7.30 interview as he defends Hanson
items.description: The One Nation senator says Pauline Hanson's meeting with far-right British activist Tommy Robinson did not amount to an endorsement of his criminal conduct, rejecting suggestions she had crossed a "red line". The otherwise serious 7.30 interview was twice interrupted by Mr Joyce's dog, prompting him to yell at it to "sit down".

items.title: Andy Burnham becomes British PM, provides AUKUS hints in first speech
items.description: Andy Burnham has pledged to provide immediate cost-of-living relief for Brits and invited US President Donald Trump to Manchester in the hours after becoming UK PM on Monday.

items.title: Iran-backed Houthis declare maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia
items.description: In a statement, the Houthis' military spokesperson Yahya Saree says the group will enforce the blockade against its "criminal Saudi enemy", effective immediately.

items.title: US launches new strikes as Trump says Iran will 'pay' for soldiers' deaths
items.description: The United States has launched a new wave of strikes on Iran after identifying two soldiers killed while defending against Iranian missile and drone attacks in Jordan.

items.title: Firebombed synagogue community to address royal commission
items.description: The community from Melbourne's Adass Israel Synagogue will provide evidence at the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion today.

items.title: Shared lifestyle might be clue to why some couples have higher dementia risk
items.description: Having a spouse with dementia puts you at a higher risk of developing the condition, a new study finds.

items.title: Israel criticises Labor's draft Palestine policy ahead of party conference
items.description: Israel's embassy has released a lengthy complaint ahead of Labor's national conference on the party's proposed position on Israel and Palestine.

items.title: Albanese would 'have a disagreement' with his younger self now
items.description: From left-wing roots to "radical centre" prime minister, Anthony Albanese reflects on his 30-year career in Parliament House.

items.title: Stubborn stigma fuelling shocking violence against sex workers in Australia
items.description: A new inquiry into violence against sex workers in Australia and Thailand comes just weeks after the murder of Thai teenager Tunchanok Donhomla, allegedly by an Australian man.

items.title: With five years gone, experts say 'not a second to lose' on Olympic build
items.description: Broken promises and scarcely broken ground. Five years since Brisbane secured the 2032 Olympic Games, this is the state of play.

items.title: Man charged with murder of UK politician Ann Widdecombe
items.description: Joshua Kerry, 28, will appear in court on Tuesday, UK time, after the death of the prominent conservative politician in her home earlier in July.

items.title: Why 'narcissist' bosses are more likely to oppose work from home
items.description: Research published last month found narcissistic leaders — those with a tendency to be self-centred and entitled — were more likely than others to resist remote work. Why? The study concluded "it interferes with their motivations for power and status".

items.title: Quiz: How well do you remember these Australian kids' TV shows?
items.description: What was the name of the tough, mangy cat in The Ferals? And which show featured EC, the faceless doll?

items.title: The musical journey of royal wedding cellist Sheku Kanneh-Mason
items.description: Sheku Kanneh-Mason went viral performing at Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's wedding. He's captivated audiences since and is touring Australia this month.

items.title: Moscow targeted by drones while Russia bombards Kyiv
items.description: Ukraine launches its latest attack on the Russian capital, firing more than 400 drones, while the Kremlin deploys more ballistic missiles against targets across Ukraine.

items.title: India's 'cockroach' movement supporters caned by police
items.description: Thousands of supporters of India's youth-led "cockroach" movement gathered in New Delhi to march ‌on parliament seeking the resignation of the education minister, despite police denying permission for the protest.

items.title: 'Good night, sweet dreams': Derryn Hinch farewelled at state funeral
items.description: Broadcaster Ray Martin, Australian actress Jacki Weaver and performer Rhonda Burchmore are among the entertainment heavyweights to pay tribute to Derryn Hinch at his state funeral service.

items.title: Taxpayers fork out almost $35,000 for MPs to stay at Queensland parliament
items.description: It has been revealed in budget estimates that 191 total overnight stays were reported by MPs last financial year, up from just 39 the previous year.

items.title: Hundreds march on Pine Gap in secretive site's biggest protest in decades
items.description: About 300 people have marched on Pine Gap in Alice Springs, protesting against its role in US military operations, in the largest protest at the top-secret defence site since 1987.

items.title: Critical beeding breakthrough welcome news for lovers of purple passionfruit
items.description: An unpalatable future has been averted for Australians who love purple-skinned passionfruit, with new research ensuring better prospects for the delicious fruit.

items.title: Underwater gardening helping to restore Tasmania's lost kelp forests
items.description: A new live-in internship program on the Tasman Peninsula is working to repopulate the area's endangered giant kelp forests through underwater gardening.

items.title: Glitter in 'beautiful big nugget of rhino poo' unlocks fertility clues
items.description: Edible glitter is being used to track the reproductive cycles of the two youngest southern white rhinos at Monarto Safari Park.
